 Trigeminal neuralgia or tic douloureux is a most common form of neuralgia that occurs due to the inflammation or compression of trigeminal nerve by an artery or a vein that frequently causes severe facial pain. It mostly affects the elderly people and generally affects right side of the face. The facial pain may occur after every few hours, minutes and seconds. 
 (Trigeminal nerve is the fifth and largest cranial nerve that is responsible for facial sensation and transmit the sensation from the brain to mouth, teeth, face and nose.)

sections.symptoms_of_trigeminal_neuralgia:
Occasional twinges of mild to moderate pain 
 Onset of severe, shooting, throbbing pain like electric shock 
 Bouts of pain lasting from a few seconds to several days, weeks, months or longer 
 Pain focused in one spot or spread in a wider pattern 
 Attacks becoming more frequent and intense over time 
 Pain affecting one side of your face at a time 
 Pain in areas managed by the trigeminal nerve, including the cheek, jaw, teeth, gums, lips, or less often the eye and forehead
sections.complications_of_trigeminal_neuralgia:
The pain can be severe and distressing. If untreated, pain may cause depression. Irritation or anxiety. 
 Patient may neglect brushing teeth or eating or drinking due to the fear of triggering the pain. This can lead to weight loss, weakness and poor oral hygiene. 
 In most cases where neuralgia is caused due to pressure from a blood vessel, there are no complications affecting the trigeminal nerve or affecting the brain. 
 In rare cases where trigeminal neuralgia occurs as a result of another condition, then various other symptoms and problems of that condition may develop. For example, as mentioned, a rare cause of neuralgia is multiple sclerosis. In this situation, other symptoms and problems associated with multiple sclerosis are likely to develop.

 Trigeminal neuralgia is correlated to Anantvaat in Ayurveda. This is a typical vata vyadhi means vata among all three doshas is aggravated and cause blockage of channels around face and head.
